title: Dynamic protrusions mediate crawling motility in Asgard archaea.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Europe PMC: not open access, no PMCID, no supplement, no accessions, no NCBI links. Read the data availability statement in the bioRxiv preprint (10.1101/2025.11.30.690169). Opened the PRIDE (proteomics repository) record PXD068820 metadata: it is a small actin co-immunoprecipitation mass-spectrometry experiment (pulling down proteins that bind actin, with IgG beads as controls), not motility data. A Zenodo search found nothing for this paper.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Cell counts (117 migrating cells from 9 cultures; 115 protrusions from 28 experiments; 46 cells / 220 protrusions; 21 M. peptidophilum cells), the semi-manual kymograph speed measurement (speed read off a time-versus-position image along a hand-drawn line), and the statement that raw microscopy is available only on request, all come from the bioRxiv preprint text. The Nature page redirected to a login and was not read.

a1_downloadable.note: Preprint data statement: raw microscopy is 'available from the first and corresponding author upon request'. Only per-figure source-data tables (not opened) and an unrelated proteomics deposit (PXD068820, metadata checked) are public.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: No labelled table exists. Any label (protrusion speed, crawling vs not, inhibitor vs control) would have to be built from the videos by tracking or manual kymographs. Source-data tables hold summary values per figure only (paper text; not opened).

a3_inputs_present.note: The inputs would be time-lapse videos, and these are withheld (available on request only).

a4_units_stated.note: Speeds are reported in µm/min in the abstract and preprint; not checked in any file.

a5_enough_rows.note: The largest unit reported is 220 protrusions or 117 tracked cells, from 9–13 cultures (preprint text). That is far below 400 even for classification.

a6_fits_laptop.note: The source tables would be tiny. Raw video size is unknown and the videos are withheld.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Could not check: there are no files to count.

a8_label_provenance.note: Speeds are measured from the microscopy by semi-manual kymography, so they are not another model's output. No downloadable table exists, though.

honest_claim_h3: Not reached: the project failed Part A.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use time-lapse microscopy of archaeal cells to classify whether a cell is crawling and how fast its protrusions extend.
plain_idea.train_on: Live-cell microscopy videos of two Asgard archaea species (Asgard archaea are the closest known microbial relatives of complex cells). Roughly 117 tracked cells and 220 protrusions, per the preprint; the videos themselves are only available on request.
plain_idea.predict: Crawling vs non-crawling, protrusion speed in µm/min, or actin-inhibitor-treated vs control. The true answers would come from the authors' kymographs: speed read off a time-versus-position image traced by hand along each protrusion.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Automated tracking could help archaea cell biologists measure shape changes at scale. But with about a hundred cells from one lab and the videos withheld, the dataset cannot support a model.

ml_idea: Classify cell motility state or regress protrusion speed from live-cell videos. Not viable: the videos are on request only and there are about 100–220 examples.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated: the project failed Part A before any data was available.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Read the data availability statement. It says raw microscopy is available on request, which kills A1.

verdict_reason: Fails A1, A2, A3 and A5. Raw microscopy videos are available only on request. There is no labelled table, only figure source data. About 117 cells or 220 protrusions is far too few. The only public deposit, PRIDE PXD068820, is an unrelated actin pull-down proteomics experiment.
